prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Houston for AC repair?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” HVAC company for AC repair in Houston — the right choice depends on your exact location, whether the job is residential or commercial, how quickly you need service, your budget, and whether you want a one-off repair or a long-term service relationship. I can help you find the best option for your situation if you tell me your ZIP code/neighborhood and whether this is an emergency.

Meanwhile, here’s a quick, practical plan you can use right away:

1. Give me your location and needs
- ZIP code or neighborhood
- Residential or commercial
- Is it an emergency (no cooling right now)?

2. How to evaluate companies (checklist)
- Licensing & certifications: ask for the contractor’s license/registration and whether technicians are NATE-certified (North American Technician Excellence) or have manufacturer training.
- Insurance: verify general liability and workers’ comp.
- Reviews & references: check Google, Yelp, BBB, and ask for local references.
- Written estimate: get a written diagnosis and price before work begins, including parts, labor, permits and taxes.
- Warranty: ask for parts and labor warranty length and what’s excluded.
- Diagnostic fee policy: will the fee be waived if you proceed with the repair?
- Upfront pricing: ask whether they charge flat-rate or hourly and whether they provide a written scope.
- Availability & response time: emergency/after-hours fees and typical arrival window.
- Permits: who pulls required permits (contractor should handle).
- Maintenance plans: if you want ongoing service, ask about tune-up plans and priority scheduling.

3. Questions to ask when you call (quick script)
- “Are you licensed/registered in Houston/Harris County? Can you give the license number?”
- “Are your technicians NATE-certified or manufacturer-trained for my system?”
- “Do you carry liability insurance and workers’ comp?”
- “What will the diagnostic fee be, and is it waived if I approve repairs?”
- “What warranty do you provide on parts and labor?”
- “Can you provide a written estimate before work starts?”
- “When can you come? Is emergency service available?”

4. Quick safety tips if your AC is down in hot weather
- Use fans, close blinds/curtains, run ceiling fans, stay hydrated.
- Move vulnerable family members/pets to a cooler location if needed.
- If you smell gas or suspect a refrigerant leak, turn off the system and call a professional immediately.

If you want, give me your ZIP code and whether you need same-day service and I’ll suggest several well-reviewed Houston HVAC companies and help you compare them (or help you evaluate any specific companies you’ve found).
